title: Dakila Onion (Dakila F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Dakila onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety from East West Seed. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Dakila onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety, also sold or known as Dakila F1 or Dakila red onion. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed.

heroImage.alt: Onion plants in beds separated by grassy paths on a Philippine farm, the kind of farm where Dakila onion is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Dakila F1 or Dakila red onion, this is the same onion. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [onion variety finder](/crop-varieties/onion), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for onion and garlic](/land-preparation/onion-garlic-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Yield, by the seller's count: at least 30 percent above open pollinated onions in the company's trials (company figure). No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit onion fields most often: [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [onion armyworm](/pests/onion-armyworm), [purple blotch of onion](/diseases/purple-blotch), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** At least 30 percent above open pollinated onions in the company's trials (company figure).
**Fruit:** Bulb: large, very even red creole bulbs with a three layered skin that store well.
Farmer cooperators in Mindoro cut their fertilizer cost by half or more and watered every 10 to 14 days instead of every 7, the company reports.
The seed carries a coating that guards the seedlings for their first 21 days.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: launched by East West as its first hybrid of the red creole type for the Philippines, and shown to over 900 farmers at a Mindoro field day in March 2026. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual onion on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Dakila onion

Red onion stores longer, while yellow onion yields more. Pick a variety that bulbs in the short days of the Philippine dry season, and plant it after the rains so the bulbs dry well. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Dakila F1 the same as Dakila?
items.a: Yes. Dakila F1 is another name for Dakila. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Dakila?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
